title: The Blue Counter
verdict: Cassian Nash was responsible for the disappearance of a Civil War diary.
intent: Cassian Nash wanted to hide a diary passage that contradicted a family legend.
The culprit needed delayed discovery so the object could pass the first search and be recovered later.
action_schema: Use role-specific access: the inventory chair reassigned volunteers during the flicker.
Remove a Civil War diary from its checked location.
Hide the item in a false-bottom document chest.
Allow incomplete suspicion to fall on distractor suspects.
evidence_cues: a Civil War diary disappeared from a historical society attic during an inventory day.
The object was confirmed present before the relevant disturbance.
The disappearance occurred within a narrow time window because the attic lights flickered when the inventory team changed rooms.
The physical trace was brown paper dust near the false-bottom chest.
The relevant tool or mechanism was a brass crate opener with old paper dust.
The item could be concealed in a false-bottom document chest.
The hiding place required insider knowledge because only the inventory chair knew the document chest had a false bottom.
The access pattern mattered because the inventory chair reassigned volunteers during the flicker.
The motive was to hide a diary passage that contradicted a family legend.
distractor_cues: a collector asking to buy artifacts
A visible conflict is suspicious but insufficient without timing and mechanism.
A bulky object or nervous behavior is insufficient unless it explains the hidden container.
